title: Beatrix and the Well
premise: August Montrose, a hospice nurse who hears the dying count backwards from a number only they can see, has spent years keeping herself small: lights on, doors counted, no attachments. When an excavation crew unearths a door sealed from the inside beneath the town's oldest well, the backwards counting spreads to the living, and August realizes she was marked at birth as the ritual's final vessel. The founders of Hollow Creek built the well to bargain with something beneath the frost—a thing that grants survival at the cost of self—and every generation it collects what it is owed. To save the town and her own name, August must complete the interrupted ritual on her own terms, surrendering not her life but her invisibility, becoming fully seen by the thing below even if it unmakes who she was.
about_author: Lior Galloway is the pen name of a former night-shift caregiver who writes horror in the margins of long vigils. They live somewhere cold, keep their doors counted, and insist the backwards numbers are just a story.

chapters.title: The Counting Ward
chapters.summary: August Montrose tends to dying Mr. Ellery, who counts backwards from forty-one with perfect calm while she keeps the lights on and recites her private rituals of doors and locks. POV: August. Emotional beat: the eerie comfort of routine, and the first crack in it—Ellery reaches zero and smiles before he dies.

chapters.title: What the Excavator Found
chapters.summary: The crew digging the new community center foundation unearths a stone door beneath the old well site, its iron ring fused, its seams sealed from within. Foreman Dana Kesh notices frost blooming in July. POV: Dana. Emotional beat: professional pride curdling into unease as the crew's radios fill with faint counting.

chapters.title: Doors Counted
chapters.summary: August takes a temp assignment at the excavation site's field office and recognizes the sound under the workers' chatter: someone alive, counting backwards. She lies to herself that it's nothing. POV: August. Emotional beat: denial; her rituals tighten into compulsions as the town's dogs go silent.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: Dana finds a ledger in the historical society archive listing every founding family of Hollow Creek and a column labeled 'Remainder.' The last entry, 1897, reads 'unfinished—vessel withheld.' POV: Dana. Emotional beat: dread of inheritance; her own family name appears eleven times.

chapters.title: Frost in July
chapters.summary: Frost patterns spread across windows in concentric rings centered on the well site. A crew member, Petey, begins counting backwards mid-conversation and doesn't remember doing it. POV: Petey. Emotional beat: loss of control over one's own mouth; the town starts avoiding eye contact.

chapters.title: Sealed From the Inside
chapters.summary: August visits the door at night and presses her palm to the stone; something on the other side presses back, patient as a held breath. She hears her own voice among the counters. POV: August. Emotional beat: recognition—the thing knows her, has always known her.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Kept Records
chapters.summary: In the archive, August finds photographs of a 19th-century nurse, Adaline Voss, whose face is her own. Voss's marginalia describes 'the Well's arithmetic' and a ritual left half-finished to spare a child. POV: August. Emotional beat: identity shaken; she was the spared child's descendant, the withheld vessel.

chapters.title: Zero Hour
chapters.summary: Petey reaches zero at his sister's kitchen table and stops—not dead, but emptied, speaking only in other people's voices. The town panics; the county sends no one; phones ring backward. POV: Dana. Emotional beat: isolation; Hollow Creek realizes it is alone with this.

chapters.title: The Bargain Explained
chapters.summary: The historical society's last elder, Ruth Calloway, explains the founders' covenant: the Well grants the town survival through hard winters, and each generation pays in selves—one person, gradually unwritten. The ritual must be finished or refused entirely. POV: Ruth. Emotional beat: terrible clarity; survival has always had a price tag.

chapters.title: Lights On
chapters.summary: August fortifies her apartment against the spreading frost, but the counting comes through the walls now, and her own reflection mouths numbers a half-second ahead of her. POV: August. Emotional beat: paranoia; the boundary between her mind and the Well dissolving.

chapters.title: The Crew Descends
chapters.summary: Against August's warning, Dana leads three volunteers to breach the door with a cutting torch. The seal resists, then opens inward onto stairs going down farther than the town's foundations should allow. POV: Dana. Emotional beat: hubris and courage tangled; one volunteer turns back, weeping.

chapters.title: Below the Frost Line
chapters.summary: In the dark beneath, Dana finds the founders' ritual chamber: thirteen alcoves, twelve holding desiccated figures arranged like sleeping guests, the thirteenth empty and shaped for someone standing. POV: Dana. Emotional beat: awe curdling to horror; the empty alcove fits August exactly.

chapters.title: What Came Back Up
chapters.summary: Two of the four return, wrong—counting forwards now, smiling too widely, calling everyone by childhood nicknames they couldn't know. The town locks them out. POV: Petey (partially restored). Emotional beat: grief for the taken; the impossibility of rescue.

chapters.title: Adaline's Refusal
chapters.summary: Voss's hidden journal reveals she broke the ritual in 1897 to save an infant, dooming the town to a century of deferred payment. The Well does not forget; it compounds interest. POV: August reading. Emotional beat: inherited guilt; anger at the ancestor who chose her for this.

chapters.title: The Town That Counts
chapters.summary: Half of Hollow Creek now counts in their sleep, audible through the walls in a chorus that rises each night toward some shared zero. Ruth Calloway reaches her number and walks calmly into the well shaft. POV: Dana. Emotional beat: communal surrender; watching neighbors choose the abyss.

chapters.title: Negotiating With Winter
chapters.summary: August descends alone to the threshold and speaks to the presence directly. It offers her the old terms: survive, be safe, be no one. She counter-offers—she will finish the ritual, but as herself, seen, named. POV: August. Emotional beat: defiance; claiming identity as a weapon rather than hiding it.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Alcove
chapters.summary: August begins the ritual in the empty alcove while Dana holds the door above, reading Voss's instructions aloud against the rising chorus. The frost writes its final pattern across the ceiling—her own name. POV: alternating August/Dana. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Seen
chapters.summary: At the ritual's crux, the Well shows August every version of herself she could have been—the invisible lives she might have lived—and demands she choose one to keep. She refuses all of them and stands in full view of the thing below. POV: August. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh; being witnessed as both wound and salvation.

chapters.title: The Reckoning
chapters.summary: The Well takes its payment: not August's life but her erasure from the town's memory and records, the price inverted—survival purchased with remembrance instead of oblivion. The counters fall silent mid-number. The door seals itself, this time from the outside. POV: Dana. Emotional beat: victory laced with loss; the town wakes remembering everything except her.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Spring comes early. The excavated site is quietly filled with concrete. Dana, the only one who somehow still remembers August, leaves flowers at an unmarked grave and finds Voss's journal blank except for one new line: 'paid in full.' POV: Dana. Emotional beat: mourning without a body; loyalty as resistance.

chapters.title: The Nurse Who Hears
chapters.summary: A new hospice nurse arrives in Hollow Creek and mentions, offhand, that the dying sometimes count backwards. She keeps her lights on and her doors counted. In the staff photo, there is a blur where a thirteenth person might stand. POV: ambiguous new arrival. Emotional beat: cyclical dread; the price survives the payer.

chapters.title: Beatrix and the Well
chapters.summary: Final chapter reveals August's true name—Beatrix, the name Voss withheld in 1897—as she persists in the space between memory and record, tending the threshold so the Well stays fed and the town stays whole. She is no longer invisible; she is the one who watches back. POV: Beatrix/August. Emotional beat: bittersweet transcendence; identity reclaimed at the cost of belonging.
